shared_elements: low-relief carving on a dressed limestone pillar face
bird-like creature shown in profile with prominent beak/head
long sinuous curved line running across the surface (snake-like)
flat, uncarved background field with figures raised slightly above it
justification: Both are shallow, flat-topped relief carvings on the same kind of pale sandy stone slab, and both include a simplified profile bird with a heavy head/beak alongside angular geometric marks and a long sinuous line, which is a fairly specific overlap in vocabulary and technique. The decisive difference is density and organisation: B packs its motifs into stacked horizontal registers (arched forms above a hatched band above a row of creatures), whereas A is a sparse, near-empty field with one creature and a couple of isolated lines, so the compositional schemes do not correspond.
